transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Well, I guess what brings me in is... I got pretty worked up in a staff meeting at work recently. I started acting out a whole fall-prevention drill right there in the room. I was moving chairs around and waving my arms all over the place to show them, and I just couldn't seem to stop doing it, even when folks told me to sit down. So, they said I needed to come in and talk to someone.

When did you first notice that you were having trouble controlling your movements or actions like this? Was this something that just started happening recently, or have you been dealing with this kind of thing for a long time?

Well, it's been going on for about... I'd say a year and five months now. It started right around the time we got a new supervisor. He started criticizing my work a lot, and then he took away these safety briefings I used to lead. That's when I first started having trouble like this.

When you were moving your arms and rearranging the chairs in that meeting, did it feel like you were doing it on purpose to demonstrate the drill, or did it feel like your body was moving on its own without you really controlling it?

Well, I was doing it on purpose, I think. Like, I was trying to show them the drill, but... once I started, I just couldn't stop. It was like I had to keep going with the chairs and the waving. Even when they told me to sit down and stop, I just kept doing it. So I was deciding to do it at first, but then I couldn't seem to turn it off.
During this past year and a half, have you ever experienced beliefs that others were out to get you, or have you heard voices or seen things that others around you couldn't hear or see?

No, I haven't heard any voices or seen things that aren't there. But... I do have this feeling that people are out to get me at work. Even when I'm just feeling regular and calm, I'm still pretty sure my supervisor and a couple of the other aides are keeping notes on me. It feels like they're always testing me, you know, making these little comments to try and prove I'm not safe to be around the seniors we take care of. It just feels like they're watching my every move.

Over this past year and a half, have there been times when you felt unusually happy, energetic, or like you had a lot more energy than normal — times when you needed much less sleep than usual but still felt great, or when your thoughts seemed to be racing?

Yeah, there are definitely times like that. There are stretches where I just feel... really bright and fired up, you know? Like everything is finally lining up perfectly and I have all this energy. But the thing is, during those times, if someone slows me down or questions what I'm doing, I get really irritable. I end up snapping at them a lot harder than I mean to.

When you have these times where you feel really bright and fired up with lots of energy, how long do they typically last? Are we talking about a few hours, a day or two, or do they go on for weeks at a time?

Well, it's not just a day or two. When I get like that—you know, feeling really energized, barely sleeping, and trying to get all my big plans going—it lasts a while. These stretches have been coming and going for about 11 months now. They definitely go on for weeks at a time before I finally crash.

Between these times when you feel really energized and fired up, do you experience periods where your mood drops significantly—where you feel sad, hopeless, or lose interest in things you normally enjoy?

No, I don't really get like that. I don't have times where I feel super sad or down in the dumps, or hopeless, like you're saying. It's really just those times with all the energy, and then just... feeling regular, I guess. I don't really lose interest in things or get depressed.

During those times when you're not feeling energized and fired up—when you're just feeling regular—do you notice changes in your sleep, appetite, or energy levels? Like, do you sleep more than usual, or eat less, or feel kind of tired or sluggish?

No, I don't really notice any of that. When I'm just feeling regular... everything is pretty much normal. My sleep goes back to a regular schedule, and I eat fine. I don't feel sluggish or dragged down or anything like that. It's really just... a normal day, I guess. Nothing out of the ordinary.

You mentioned these energized stretches last for weeks at a time. During the shortest of these periods when you felt that way, how many days would you say it lasted before things settled back to normal?

I'm not really sure about an exact number of days, to be honest. I never really counted them on a calendar or anything. 

I just know it's always at least a couple of weeks. So maybe... I don't know, fourteen days or so for the shortest one? It's never just a quick few days, it's always a solid stretch before I finally settle down and go back to regular.

You mentioned the shortest energized stretch lasted at least a couple of weeks. But I want to make sure I'm clear: have you ever had one of these energized, high-energy periods that lasted only 3 or 4 days, or has every single one of them always lasted at least a week or longer?
No, I've never had one that was just three or four days. It's... it's always longer than that. Every single time, it's been at least a week, usually longer, like I said. Never just a few days.
